title: ICSE CLASS 2 — Environmental Studies | Pollution Prevention
description: Subject-wise test on Pollution Prevention (Environmental Studies) for ICSE CLASS 2. 25Q.
subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these causes air pollution?

options.explanation: Planting trees helps to clean the air.
Smoke released from factories contains harmful gases that mix with the air, making it dirty and causing air pollution.
Raining heavily helps to clean the air and does not cause pollution.
Children playing in a park does not cause air pollution.

questions.explanation: Smoke released from factories contains harmful gases that mix with the air, making it dirty and causing air pollution.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: What is the best way to dispose of garbage from our homes?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the road causes land pollution.
Burning garbage in the open causes air pollution.
Putting garbage in a dustbin ensures it is collected and processed properly, preventing land and water pollution.
Throwing garbage in a river causes water pollution.

questions.explanation: Putting garbage in a dustbin ensures it is collected and processed properly, preventing land and water pollution.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: How can we save water while brushing our teeth?

options.explanation: Keeping the tap running wastes water.
Using a lot of water is wasteful.

options.text: Turn off the tap while scrubbing
options.explanation: Turning off the tap while scrubbing saves a significant amount of water that would otherwise be wasted.

options.text: Brush for a very long time
options.explanation: Brushing for a very long time does not necessarily save water.

questions.explanation: Turning off the tap while scrubbing saves a significant amount of water that would otherwise be wasted.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Why is it good to plant more trees?

options.explanation: Trees do not give us loud music.
Trees help to clean the air, not make it dirty.

options.text: They help to clean the air
options.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which helps to clean the air we breathe.
Trees do not make the ground muddy.

questions.explanation: Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, which helps to clean the air we breathe.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Throwing plastic bags and waste into a river causes which type of pollution?

options.explanation: Throwing waste into a river does not directly cause air pollution.
Throwing waste into a river does not cause noise pollution.
When waste is thrown into rivers, it contaminates the water, making it dirty and harmful for aquatic life and human use.
Throwing waste into a river does not directly cause land pollution.

questions.explanation: When waste is thrown into rivers, it contaminates the water, making it dirty and harmful for aquatic life and human use.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Listening to very loud music or horns honking loudly can cause:

options.explanation: Loud music or horns honking loudly does not cause air pollution.
Excessive or unwanted sound is known as noise pollution, which can be harmful to hearing and overall well-being.
Loud music or horns honking loudly does not cause water pollution.
Loud music or horns honking loudly does not cause land pollution.

questions.explanation: Excessive or unwanted sound is known as noise pollution, which can be harmful to hearing and overall well-being.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Which of these actions helps to prevent pollution?

options.text: Burning dry leaves and plastic in the garden
options.explanation: Burning dry leaves and plastic in the garden causes air pollution.

options.text: Using a car for very short distances
options.explanation: Using a car for very short distances can cause air pollution.

options.text: Carrying a reusable cloth bag for shopping
options.explanation: Using reusable cloth bags reduces the need for single-use plastic bags, which are a major cause of land and water pollution.

options.text: Throwing food wrappers anywhere after eating
options.explanation: Throwing food wrappers anywhere after eating causes land pollution.

questions.explanation: Using reusable cloth bags reduces the need for single-use plastic bags, which are a major cause of land and water pollution.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Why is it harmful to cut down many trees?

options.text: It makes the sky look clearer.
options.explanation: Cutting down trees does not make the sky look clearer.

options.text: It helps to make more roads.
options.explanation: Cutting down trees is not necessary to make more roads.

options.text: It makes the air dirtier and causes floods.
options.explanation: Trees clean the air and their roots hold the soil, preventing erosion and floods. Cutting them down makes the air dirtier and increases the risk of flooding.

options.text: It helps animals find new homes.
options.explanation: Cutting down trees can harm animals' habitats.

questions.explanation: Trees clean the air and their roots hold the soil, preventing erosion and floods. Cutting them down makes the air dirtier and increases the risk of flooding.

questions.question: Read the two statements: Statement 1: We should walk or cycle for short distances instead of using a car. Statement 2: Walking and cycling do not produce smoke and keep the air clean. Which of the following is true?

options.text: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false.
options.explanation: Both statements are true.

options.text: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true.
options.explanation: Both statements are true.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true, and Statement 2 explains Statement 1.
options.explanation: Walking and cycling are eco-friendly ways to travel for short distances because they do not release harmful smoke, thus helping to keep the air clean.

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are true, but Statement 2 does not explain Statement 1.
options.explanation: Statement 2 explains why Statement 1 is true.

questions.explanation: Walking and cycling are eco-friendly ways to travel for short distances because they do not release harmful smoke, thus helping to keep the air clean.

questions.question: Rina saw her neighbour throwing all their kitchen waste, like fruit peels and vegetable scraps, directly into the street. What is a better way for her neighbour to manage this waste to help prevent pollution?

options.text: Collect it and burn it in a small fire.
options.explanation: Burning kitchen waste can cause air pollution.

options.text: Throw it into the nearest pond.
options.explanation: Throwing kitchen waste into a pond can cause water pollution.

options.text: Put it in a compost pit to make manure for plants.
options.explanation: Kitchen waste like fruit peels and vegetable scraps are biodegradable and can be turned into nutrient-rich compost, which is good for plants and prevents land pollution.

options.text: Ask a friend to throw it in their garden.
options.explanation: Asking a friend to throw kitchen waste in their garden is not a responsible way to manage waste.

questions.explanation: Kitchen waste like fruit peels and vegetable scraps are biodegradable and can be turned into nutrient-rich compost, which is good for plants and prevents land pollution.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a cause of air pollution?

options.explanation: Smoke from factories releases harmful gases into the air, causing air pollution.
Smoke from vehicles releases harmful gases into the air, causing air pollution.
Fresh air from trees is clean and helps reduce pollution, not cause it.
Burning garbage releases harmful gases into the air, causing air pollution.

questions.explanation: Fresh air from trees is clean and helps reduce pollution, not cause it. Smoke from factories, vehicles, and burning garbage all release harmful gases into the air.

questions.question: What is the best way to dispose of garbage to prevent land pollution?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the road contributes to land pollution.
Dumping garbage in a river contributes to water pollution.
Putting garbage in a dustbin ensures it is collected and processed properly, preventing land pollution.

options.text: Burn it in an open field
options.explanation: Burning garbage in an open field contributes to air pollution.

questions.explanation: Putting garbage in a dustbin ensures it is collected and processed properly, preventing it from littering the land and causing pollution.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: If you see a tap running unnecessarily, what should you do to prevent water wastage?

options.explanation: Ignoring a running tap wastes water.
Playing with the water wastes more water.

options.text: Tell your friend to play with it
options.explanation: Telling a friend to play with the water wastes more water.
Turning off the tap conserves water and prevents wastage.

questions.explanation: Turning off a running tap immediately is the correct action to conserve water and prevent wastage.
questions.subject: icse2-evs

questions.question: Why should we avoid throwing plastic bags into rivers or lakes?

options.explanation: Plastic bags do not make the water colorful in a beneficial way.

options.text: Fish like to play with them.
options.explanation: Fish do not benefit from playing with plastic bags.

options.text: They harm aquatic animals and pollute water.
options.explanation: Plastic bags harm aquatic animals and pollute the water.

options.text: They make the water taste better.
options.explanation: Plastic bags do not improve the taste of the water.

questions.explanation: Plastic bags are very harmful to aquatic life, as animals can mistake them for food or get tangled in them, and they also pollute the water.

questions.question: Which of these actions helps keep our surroundings clean and prevents pollution?

options.explanation: Littering the playground contributes to pollution.
Wasting water while bathing contributes to water scarcity.
Planting more trees helps clean the air and prevents pollution.
Making loud noise contributes to noise pollution.

questions.explanation: Planting more trees helps clean the air, provides oxygen, and makes the environment greener and healthier, directly preventing pollution.

questions.question: Statement A: Loud music and vehicle horns cause noise pollution. Statement B: Noise pollution is good for our ears. Which statement is correct?

options.explanation: Statement B is incorrect because noise pollution is harmful to our ears.
Statement A is correct because loud music and horns cause noise pollution.
Both statements cannot be correct because Statement B is incorrect.
Statement A is correct, so both statements are not incorrect.

questions.explanation: Loud music and horns are indeed sources of noise pollution. Noise pollution is harmful to our ears and health, making Statement B incorrect.

questions.question: A factory owner decides to treat the waste water before releasing it into the river. This action will primarily help in preventing which type of pollution?

options.explanation: Treating waste water does not directly address air pollution.
Treating waste water prevents water pollution.
Treating waste water does not directly address noise pollution.
Treating waste water does not directly address land pollution.

questions.explanation: Treating waste water before releasing it into a river directly addresses the pollutants in the water, thus preventing water pollution.

questions.question: Your neighbour is burning dry leaves and garbage in their backyard. What kind of pollution will this cause?

options.explanation: Burning leaves and garbage does not directly cause water pollution.
Burning leaves and garbage causes air pollution.
Burning leaves and garbage does not directly cause noise pollution.
Burning leaves and garbage does not directly cause soil pollution.

questions.explanation: Burning leaves and garbage releases smoke and harmful gases into the atmosphere, which is a direct cause of air pollution.

questions.question: Rohan always carries a cloth bag when he goes shopping instead of taking new plastic bags. Why is Rohan's habit good for the environment?

options.explanation: While cloth bags may be fashionable, this is not the primary environmental benefit.

options.text: He saves money by not buying plastic bags.
options.explanation: Saving money is not the primary environmental benefit of using cloth bags.

options.text: It reduces the use of plastic, which causes pollution.
options.explanation: Using cloth bags reduces the demand for single-use plastic bags, which helps prevent pollution.

options.text: Cloth bags are lighter to carry.
options.explanation: While cloth bags may be lighter, this is not the primary environmental benefit.

questions.explanation: Using cloth bags reduces the demand for single-use plastic bags, which are a major source of land and water pollution because they do not decompose easily.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most effective way for a Class 2 student to contribute to pollution prevention at home?

options.explanation: Building a factory is not feasible for a Class 2 student and can contribute to pollution.
Driving a car is not typically something a Class 2 student can control or do.

options.text: Switching off lights and fans when leaving a room.
options.explanation: Switching off lights and fans saves electricity and reduces air pollution.

options.text: Collecting all the garbage from the city.
options.explanation: Collecting all the garbage from the city is not feasible for a Class 2 student.

questions.explanation: Switching off lights and fans saves electricity, which in turn reduces the demand for power generation (often from burning fossil fuels), thereby reducing air pollution.

questions.question: Which of these makes the air dirty and harmful for us to breathe?

options.explanation: Planting green trees helps to purify the air, not pollute it.
Smoke from factories and vehicles contains harmful gases and particles that pollute the air, making it difficult and unhealthy to breathe.
Fresh rainwater is clean and does not pollute the air.
A gentle breeze is a natural and clean phenomenon that does not pollute the air.

questions.explanation: Smoke from factories and vehicles contains harmful gases and particles that pollute the air, making it difficult and unhealthy to breathe.

questions.question: What is the best way to dispose of garbage and waste from our homes?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the street can lead to pollution and unhygienic conditions.
Using a dustbin ensures that waste is collected and managed properly, preventing it from polluting our surroundings.

options.text: Throw it into a nearby river
options.explanation: Throwing garbage into a river can lead to water pollution and harm aquatic life.
Leaving garbage in the garden can lead to pollution and unhygienic conditions.

questions.explanation: Using a dustbin ensures that waste is collected and managed properly, preventing it from polluting our surroundings.

questions.question: Rohan saw a lot of empty plastic bottles and food wrappers lying on the ground in a park. What kind of pollution is this causing?

options.explanation: Air pollution refers to the contamination of the air, not the land.
Water pollution refers to the contamination of water, not the land.
When waste like plastic bottles and wrappers is left on the ground, it pollutes the land, making it dirty and harmful for plants and animals.
Noise pollution refers to the contamination of the environment by excessive noise, not the land.

questions.explanation: When waste like plastic bottles and wrappers is left on the ground, it pollutes the land, making it dirty and harmful for plants and animals.

questions.question: Which of the following actions helps to keep our environment clean and prevent pollution?

options.explanation: Burning dry leaves and garbage can lead to air pollution and unhygienic conditions.

options.text: Throwing fruit peels on the road
options.explanation: Throwing fruit peels on the road can lead to pollution and unhygienic conditions.

options.text: Using a cloth bag instead of a plastic bag for shopping
options.explanation: Using cloth bags reduces the use of plastic, which is a major pollutant and takes a very long time to decompose, thus helping to prevent land pollution.

options.text: Wasting water by leaving taps open
options.explanation: Wasting water can lead to water scarcity and pollution.

questions.explanation: Using cloth bags reduces the use of plastic, which is a major pollutant and takes a very long time to decompose, thus helping to prevent land pollution.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good habit to prevent pollution?

options.text: Turning off lights and fans when leaving a room
options.explanation: Turning off lights and fans when leaving a room helps to conserve energy and reduce pollution.

options.text: Planting more saplings in your locality
options.explanation: Planting more saplings helps to purify the air and reduce pollution.

options.text: Throwing all kinds of waste, including old batteries, into one regular dustbin
options.explanation: Throwing old batteries and other electronic waste into a regular dustbin is not a good habit because these items contain harmful chemicals that can leak out and cause severe land and water pollution.

options.text: Carrying a reusable water bottle to school
options.explanation: Carrying a reusable water bottle helps to reduce plastic waste and pollution.

questions.explanation: Throwing old batteries and other electronic waste into a regular dustbin is not a good habit because these items contain harmful chemicals that can leak out and cause severe land and water pollution.
